items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: Voice of the Theater, with JBL’s.

ctx.x: And then at the end of the night you get to tear — © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -21-

And you get to tear it all down at the end. Yeah. Everybody else is like drunk and leaving and you’re like, “uh guys?” No by that time we had people that would help. But that was a great time. There’s like all these old photographs. And one guy cut together a YouTube. We made a cassette recording of the day and it actually came out great. So that’s still out there, you see it on YouTube and it’s got like — there’s this one, all the elms had died so the quad was wide open. It was like right outside South dorm is…

It’s really cool because I’ve interviewed a few Hamilton folks from the classes of the 50’s. And they were doing the same thing, except they were playing Dixieland, they were playing upbeat jazz, but they were playing the frat parties, they would drive to Cornell to a couple of frats and all this stuff. That’s really neat.
